name: damageCategoryCode
title: Damage Category Code
description: The code that specifies the overall category of facilities or work completed for a project. Emergency work category codes: Category A: Debris Removal - Clearance of trees and woody debris; certain building wreckage; damaged/destroyed building contents; sand, mud, silt, and gravel; vehicles; and other disaster-related material deposited on public and, in very limited cases, private property .Category B: Emergency Protective Measures - Measures taken before, during, and after a disaster to eliminate/reduce an immediate threat to life, public health, or safety - or to eliminate/reduce an immediate threat of significant damage to improved public and private property through cost-effective measures. Permanent work damage category Codes: Category C - Roads and Bridges Repair of roads, bridges, and associated features, such as shoulders, ditches, culverts, lighting, and signs. Category D - Water Control Facilities Repair - Repair of drainage channels, pumping facilities, and some irrigation facilities. Repair of levees, dams, and flood control channels Category E - Buildings and Equipment Repair - Replacement of buildings, including their contents and systems; heavy equipment; and vehicles. Category F - Utilities Repair - Repair of water treatment and delivery systems; power generation facilities and distribution facilities; sewage collection and treatment facilities; and communications. Category G - Parks, Recreational Facilities, and Other Facilities Repair  - Repair and restoration of parks, playgrounds, pools, cemeteries, mass transit facilities, and beaches. This category also is used for any work or facility that cannot be characterized adequately by Categories A-F

The status of the second appeal.  The status categories are:  
 "Under Review" - FEMA has received the appeal and is actively working on it, or FEMA is waiting on information from a request for information (RFI).  A final decision has not yet been rendered. 
 "Granted" - FEMA has approved the relief requested by the applicant.  
 "Partially Granted" - FEMA has approved a portion of the relief requested by the applicant.
 "Denied" - FEMA has decided not to approve the relief requested by the applicant.
 "Withdrawn" - The applicant has notified FEMA that it wishes to withdraw its appeal.
 "Rescinded" - The FEMA Region has notified FEMA HQ that it wishes to retract its first appeal decision and reevaluate the appeal.
. "Remanded" - FEMA HQ has returned the appeal to the FEMA Region for further action.

name: eventDesignationNumber
title: Event Designation Number (EDN)
description:
The Event Designation Number (EDN) is a unique identifier established for a catastrophe flood event.
NOTE: EDN has replaced FICO as the new event tracking designation. Prior to June 2020 flood events were assigned FICO number designations; after June 2020, flood events are assigned EDN number designations. A public bulletin will designate the EDN number assignments by state with corresponding dates of loss. Example: 2 letter state abbreviation (TX), 2-digit event designator (02) and 2-digit year (20). Full example would be TX0220.

name: ficoNumber
title: Flood Insurance Claims Office (FICO) Number
description:
Number assigned at the time of a significant flooding event to uniquely identify each affected state. A public bulletin will designate the FICO number assignments by state with corresponding dates of loss. 
Note: Flood Insurance Claims Office (FICO) is an NFIP claims processing office set up in a catastrophe area when a sufficient number of flood claims result from a single event. EDN has replaced FICO as the new event tracking designation. Prior to June 2020 flood events were assigned FICO number designations; after June 2020, flood events are assigned EDN number designations. A public bulletin will designate the EDN number assignments by state with corresponding dates of loss. Example: 2 letter state abbreviation (TX), 2-digit event designator (02) and 2-digit year (20). Full example would be TX0220.

name: obstructionType
title: Obstruction Type
description:
Code that describes the type of obstruction that may be present under an elevated building. An obstruction includes an enclosed area and/or machinery and equipment attached to the building below the lowest elevated floor.
10 : Free of obstruction
15 : With obstruction: enclosure/crawlspace with proper openings not used for rating (not applicable in V Zones)
20 : With obstruction: less than 300 sq. ft. with breakaway walls, but no machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor, or the elevation of the machinery or equipment is at or above the Base Flood Elevation
24 : With obstruction: less than 300 sq. ft. with breakaway walls or finished enclosure and with machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor. The elevation of the machinery or equipment is below the Base Flood Elevation.
30 : With obstruction: 300 sq. ft. or more with breakaway walls, but no machinery or equipment attached to building below the Base Flood Elevation
34 : With obstruction: 300 sq. ft. or more with breakaway walls or finished enclosure and with machinery or equipment attached to building below the Base Flood Elevation
40 : With obstruction: no walls, but the elevation of machinery or equipment attached to building is below Base Flood Elevation
50 : With obstruction: non-breakaway walls/crawlspace or finished enclosure with no machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor
54 : With obstruction: non-breakaway walls/crawlspace or finished enclosure with machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor
60 : With obstruction
70 : With Certification subgrade crawlspace (AE, A01-A30, unnumbered A, AO, AH,AOB, AHB zones)
80 : Without Certification subgrade crawlspace (all zones)
90 : With Enclosure: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in A zones. No other enclosure below the BFE.
91 : Free of Obstruction: Elevated buildings with lattice, slats, or shutters (including louvers) enclosing the elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction or machinery and equipment (M&E) servicing the building located below the BFE. The building will be rated free of obstruction with the V zone elevator loading added to the building basic limit.
92 : With Enclosure: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in A zones. Enclosure below the BFE has no proper openings, is finished, or is used for other than parking, building access,or storage.
94 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction or machinery and equipment (M&E)servicing the building located belowthe BFE.
95 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway wall obstruction is unfinished and elevator and obstruction are located below the BFE but no machinery and equipment (M&E) servicing the building is located below the BFE.
96 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway wall obstruction is finished or is used for other than parking, building access, or storage.
97 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction, but has M&E servicing the building located below the BFE.
98 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway walls obstruction and M&E servicing the building are located below the BFE.

name: nfipRatedCommunityNumber
title: Rated NFIP Community Number
description: A six-digit designation identifying the rated NFIP community. The first two numbers are the state code. The next four are the FEMA-assigned community number. An alphabetical suffix is added to a community number to identify revisions in the FIRM for that community

name: nfipCommunityNumberCurrent
title: Current NFIP Community Number
description: A six-digit designation identifying the current NFIP community. The first two numbers are the state code. The next four are the FEMA-assigned community number. An alphabetical suffix is added to a community number to identify revisions in the FIRM for that community

name: nfipCommunityName
title: Rated NFIP Community Name
description: A local political entity that has the authority to adopt and enforce floodplain ordinances for the area under its jurisdiction.

name: obstructionType
title: Obstruction Type
description:
Code that describes the type of obstruction that may be present under an elevated building. An obstruction includes an enclosed area and/or machinery and equipment attached to the building below the lowest elevated floor.
10 : Free of obstruction
15 : With obstruction: enclosure/crawlspace with proper openings not used for rating (not applicable in V Zones)
20 : With obstruction: less than 300 sq. ft. with breakaway walls, but no machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor, or the elevation of the machinery or equipment is at or above the Base Flood Elevation
24 : With obstruction: less than 300 sq. ft. with breakaway walls or finished enclosure and with machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor. The elevation of the machinery or equipment is below the Base Flood Elevation.
30 : With obstruction: 300 sq. ft. or more with breakaway walls, but no machinery or equipment attached to building below the Base Flood Elevation
34 : With obstruction: 300 sq. ft. or more with breakaway walls or finished enclosure and with machinery or equipment attached to building below the Base Flood Elevation
40 : With obstruction: no walls, but the elevation of machinery or equipment attached to building is below Base Flood Elevation
50 : With obstruction: non-breakaway walls/crawlspace or finished enclosure with no machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor
54 : With obstruction: non-breakaway walls/crawlspace or finished enclosure with machinery or equipment attached to building below lowest elevated floor
60 : With obstruction
70 : With Certification subgrade crawlspace (AE, A01-A30, unnumbered A, AO, AH,AOB, AHB zones)
80 : Without Certification subgrade crawlspace (all zones)
90 : With Enclosure: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in A zones. No other enclosure below the BFE.
91 : Free of Obstruction: Elevated buildings with lattice, slats, or shutters (including louvers) enclosing the elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction or machinery and equipment (M&E) servicing the building located below the BFE. The building will be rated free of obstruction with the V zone elevator loading added to the building basic limit.
92 : With Enclosure: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in A zones. Enclosure below the BFE has no proper openings, is finished, or is used for other than parking, building access,or storage.
94 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction or machinery and equipment (M&E)servicing the building located belowthe BFE.
95 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway wall obstruction is unfinished and elevator and obstruction are located below the BFE but no machinery and equipment (M&E) servicing the building is located below the BFE.
96 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway wall obstruction is finished or is used for other than parking, building access, or storage.
97 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. No other obstruction, but has M&E servicing the building located below the BFE.
98 : With Obstruction: Elevated buildings with elevator below the BFE in V zones. Breakaway walls obstruction and M&E servicing the building are located below the BFE.

name: nfipRatedCommunityNumber
title: Rated NFIP Community ID Number
description: A six-digit designation identifying the rated NFIP community. The first two numbers are the state code. The next four are the FEMA-assigned community number. An alphabetical suffix is added to a community number to identify revisions in the FIRM for that community

name: nfipCommunityNumberCurrent
title: Current NFIP Community Number
description: A six-digit designation identifying the current NFIP community. The first two numbers are the state code. The next four are the FEMA-assigned community number. An alphabetical suffix is added to a community number to identify revisions in the FIRM for that community

name: nfipCommunityName
title: Rated NFIP Community Name
description: A local political entity that has the authority to adopt and enforce floodplain ordinances for the area under its jurisdiction.

name: reportedCity
title: Reported City
description: City where the insured building is located. A value of "NA" indicates the city value is currently unavailable.

name: subapplicationIdentifier
title: Subapplication Identifier
description: Single-value that uniquely identifies the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: communityName
title: Community Name
description: Name of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) community associated with the subapplication/subgrant (e.g., City of Chicago). Generally, an NFIP community represents the lowest level of government with land use authority. Thus, not every city or town is recognized as its own community with the NFIP. Each state or territory determines land use authority granted to counties/parishes/boroughs, towns/cities, tribal area, etc. within their own jurisdiction. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: county
title: County
description: Name of the County or County equivalent associated with the community (e.g., Cook County). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: stateAbbreviation
title: State Abbreviation
description: Two letter abbreviation of the State (e.g., IL represents Illinois) associated with the community. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: communityNumber
title: Community Number
description: Identifier assigned to the County or County equivalent associated with the community (e.g., 031 represents Cook County). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: countyCode
title: County Code
description: Identifier assigned to the County or County equivalent associated with the community (e.g., 031 represents Cook County). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: stateNumberCode
title: State Number Code
description: Identifier assigned to the State associated with the community (e.g., 17 represents Illinois). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: isCrsCommunity
title: Is a CRS Community
description: Indicates if the community is a CRS Community. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO]

name: crsRating
title: CRS Rating
description: CRS Rating for the community. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: congressionalDistrict
title: Congressional District
description: The Congressional District(s) associated with the community. When multiple congressional districts are present, they are separated by a ",". [Source: FEMA GO]

name: hmgpReconciliationDate
title: HMGP Reconciliation Date
description: The date FEMA Headquarters concurred on the financial reconciliation conducted by the Region and has closed the program for the disaster

name: disasterDueDateForNewApps
title: Due Date for New Applications
description: Final due date for new HMGP applications

name: disasterPopEndDate
title: Disaster Period of Performance End Date
description: The Period of Performance (POP) is the period of time during which the non-Federal entity may incur new obligations to carry out all administrative actions and award activities, and incur costs. For state management cost, the initial POP may not exceed 8 years from the disaster declaration

name: hmgpPopEndDate
title: HMGP Period of Performance End Date
description: The latest work due date or work revised date from the work scheduled across all projects within a disaster. This represents the day by which the non-Federal entity may incur new obligations to carry out all administrative actions and award activities, and incur costs

name: hmgpPopExtnDate
title: HMGP Period of Performance Extension Date
description: The day by which the non-Federal entity may incur new obligations to carry out all administrative actions and award activities, and incur costs

name: hmgpPopExtnNum
title: HMGP Period of Performance Extension Number
description: The number of the latest extension the disaster has received since the expiration of the original Period of Performance

name: liqPeriodDate
title: Liquidation Period Date
description: The Disaster Liquidation Period is the time after the grant performance period ends when a non-federal entity must liquidate all obligations incurred during the performance period

name: liqPeriodMaxDate
title: Liquidation Period Latest Extension Date
description: The date of the latest Liquidation Period Extension

name: liqPeriodMaxPopNum
title: Liquidation Period Latest Extension Number
description: The number of the latest Liquidation Period Extension

name: liqPeriodMaxExtDate
title: Additional Extension after Liquidation Period Date
description: The date of the latest additional extension granted after the Liquidation Period end date

name: cisType
title: CIS Type
description: CIS Government Unit (Derived from CIS Name)

name: liqPeriodMaxExtNum
title: Additional Extension after Liquidation Period Number
description: The number of the latest additional extension granted after the Liquidation Period end date

name: lockedInCeilingAmount
title: Locked In Ceiling Amount
description: The level of HMGP funding available in dollars to a Recipient/Grantee for a particular disaster declaration. This dollar amount, also known as the 'lock-in' value for HMGP, is the maximum that FEMA can obligate for eligible HMGP activities

name: mitigationDollarsAvailable
title: Mitigation Dollars Available
description: The remaining amount available to Recipients for eligible projects

name: obligatedTotalAmount
title: Total Amount Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for the disaster in dollars. This amount includes Recipient/Grantee and Subrecipient/Subgrantee admin costs. This field name was previously referred to as obligated total amount.

name: obligatedInitiativeAmount
title: Initative Project Amount Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for 5% initiative projects in dollars. The 5% Initiative allows Recipients/Grantees under the HMGP to use up to five percent of total HMGP grant funds for projects that are difficult to evaluate using FEMA-approved cost-effectiveness methodologies, but which otherwise meet HMGP eligibility requirements. This field name was previously referred to as obligated initiative amount.

name: obligatedPlanningAmount
title: Planning Project Amount Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for planning projects in dollars. Up to 7% of a Recipient/Grantee's HMGP funding can be used for mitigation planning related activities. This field name was previously referred to as obligated planning amount

name: obligatedRegularAmount
title: Regular Project Amount Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for regular projects in dollars. This field name was previously referred to as obligated regular amount. For more information on eligible mitigation activities, visit: https://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation

name: obligatedRecipientAdmin
title: Recipient Administrative Costs Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for Recipient Administrative Costs in dollars. Recipient Administrative Costs are provided to the Recipient for overtime pay, per diem, and travel for employees performing grant administration tasks. Recipient Administrative Costs only apply to disasters declared prior to November 13, 2007. This field name was previously referred to as Obligated Grantee Admin

name: obligatedSubrecipientAdmin
title: Subrecipient Administrative Costs Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for Subrecipient Administrative Costs in dollars. Subrecipient Administrative Costs are provided to the Subrecipient for the preparation of applications, quarterly reports, audits, related field inspections, recordkeeping, and the filing of reimbursement claims to the Recipient. Subrecipient Administrative Costs only apply to disasters declared prior to November 13, 2007. This field name was previously referred to as obligated Subgrantee Admin

name: obligatedRecipientMgmtAmt
title: Recipient Management Costs Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for Recipient Management Costs in dollars. Management Costs are any indirect costs, administrative expenses, and any other expenses not directly chargeable to a specific project that are reasonably incurred by a recipient or subrecipient in administering and managing an HMGP grant award. Recipient Management Costs only apply to disasters declared on or after August 1, 2017. This field name was previously referred to as Obligated SMC Amount

name: obligatedSubrecipMgmtAmt
title: Subrecipient Management Costs Obligated
description: Total amount obligated for Subrecipient Management Costs in dollars. Subrecipient Management Costs are any indirect costs, administrative expenses, and any other expenses not directly chargeable to a specific project that are reasonably incurred by a recipient or subrecipient in administering and managing an HMGP grant award. Subrecipient Management Costs only apply to disasters declared on or after August 1, 2017

name: pendingProjectsQuantity
title: Pending Project Quantity
description: Number of pending projects for the disaster

name: pendingFedShareProposedAmt
title: Pending Project Federal Share Proposed Amount
description: Proposed federal share of the pending projects for the disaster

name: hash
title: Hash
description: MD5 hash of fields and values of the record

name: lastRefresh
title: Last Refresh
description: Date the record was last updated in the API data store

name: id
title: ID
description: Unique ID assigned to the record

name: femaDeclarationString
title: FEMA Declaration String
description: Agency standard method for uniquely identifying Stafford Act declarations - Concatenation of declaration type, disaster number and state code. Ex: DR-4393-NC

name: cisSource
title: CIS Source
description: Source of CIS data; typically PIVOT

name: disasterNumber
title: Disaster Number
description: Sequentially assigned number used to designate an event or incident declared as a disaster.  For more information on the disaster process, please visit https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared

name: state
title: State
description: The name or phrase describing the U.S. state, district, or territory

name: declarationType
title: Declaration Type
description: Two character code that defines if this is a major disaster, fire management, or emergency declaration. For more information on the disaster process, please visit https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared

name: declarationDate
title: Declaration Date
description: Date the disaster was declared

name: fyDeclared
title: FY Declared
description: Fiscal year in which the disaster was declared

name: incidentType
title: Incident Type
description: The primary or official type of incident such as fire or flood. Secondary incident types may have been designated. See the designatedIncidentTypes field. For more information on incident types, please visit https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared.

name: declarationTitle
title: Declaration Title
description: Title for the disaster

name: ihProgramDeclared
title: IH Program Declared
description: Denotes whether the Individuals and Households program was declared for this disaster. For more information on the program, please visit https://www.fema.gov/assistance/individual/program. To determine which FEMA events have been authorized to receive Individual Assistance, use both ihProgramDeclared and iaProgramDeclared. For more information see https://www.fema.gov/about/openfema/faq

name: iaProgramDeclared
title: IA Program Declared
description: Denotes whether the Individual Assistance program was declared for this disaster. For more information on the program, please visit https://www.fema.gov/assistance/individual/program. To determine which FEMA events have been authorized to receive Individual Assistance, use both ihProgramDeclared and iaProgramDeclared. For more information see https://www.fema.gov/about/openfema/faq

name: paProgramDeclared
title: PA Program Declared
description: Denotes whether the Public Assistance program was declared for this disaster. For more information on the program, please visit https://www.fema.gov/assistance/public/program-overview

name: hmProgramDeclared
title: HM Program Declared
description: Denotes whether the Hazard Mitigation program was declared for this disaster. For more information on the program, please visit https://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation/hazard-mitigation

name: incidentBeginDate
title: Incident Begin Date
description: Date the incident itself began

name: incidentEndDate
title: Incident End Date
description: Date the incident itself ended

name: disasterCloseoutDate
title: Disaster Closeout Date
description: Date all financial transactions for all programs are completed

name: tribalRequest
title: Tribal Request
description: Denotes that a declaration request was submitted directly to the President, independently of a state, by a Tribal Nation.

name: fipsStateCode
title: FIPS State Code
description: FIPS two-digit numeric code used to identify the United States, the District of Columbia, US territories, outlying areas of the US and freely associated states

name: fipsCountyCode
title: FIPS County Code
description: FIPS three-digit numeric code used to identify counties and county equivalents in the United States, the District of Columbia, US territories, outlying areas of the US and freely associated states. Please note that Indian Reservations are not counties and thus will not have a FIPS county code, please utilize the placeCode field instead. If the designation is made for the entire state, this value will be 000 as multiple (all) counties cannot be entered.

name: placeCode
title: Place Code
description: A unique code system FEMA uses internally to recognize locations that takes the numbers '99' + the 3-digit county FIPS code. There are some declared locations that dont have recognized FIPS county codes in which case we assigned a unique identifier

name: designatedArea
title: Designated Area
description: The name or phrase describing the geographic area that was included in the declaration

name: declarationRequestNumber
title: Declaration Request Number
description: Number assigned to the declaration request

name: subapplicationIdentifier
title: Subapplication Identifier
description: Single-value that uniquely identifies the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO,  eGrants, NEMIS]

name: transactionType
title: Transaction Type
description: The type of financial transaction (i.e., Award, Amendment, Deobligation, Payment). [Source: FEMA GO, IFMIS]

name: transactionDate
title: Transaction Date
description: Date the financial transaction was processed by FEMA. While this value may contain time information (00:00:00.000), these are system generated and do not reflect the actual time associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS, IFMIS]

name: commitmentIdentifier
title: Commitment Identifier
description: Single-value that identifies the commitment identifier associated with the financial transaction. A commitment is the reservation of funds for a specific purpose and the certifying of funds availability. Commitment identifier is made up of the [Location Code][Sequentially Assigned Number][Procurement Method][Fiscal Year][Optional Characters]. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, IFMIS]

name: paymentNumber
title: Payment Number
description: Number used to represent the order of payments. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: accsLine
title: ACCS Line
description: Single-value that identifies the line of account used for the financial transaction. The Accounting Classification Code Structure (ACCS) is used to identify the expenditures for appropriated funded. The ACCS is made up of the [Budget Fiscal Year]-[Fund Code]-[Program Code]-[Organization Code]-[Project Code]-[Object Code]-[Fund Type]. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS, IFMIS]

name: fundCode
title: Fund Code
description: Single-value that identifies the source of appropriation funding for financial transaction. [Source: FEMA GO, IFMIS]

name: amount
title: Amount
description: Amount in dollars associated with the financial transaction. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS, IFMIS]

name: subapplicationIdentifier
title: Subapplication Identifier
description: Single-value that uniquely identifies the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: program
title: Program
description: Name of the Hazard Mitigation Assistance grant program (e.g., Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities grant program) associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: fiscalYear
title: Fiscal Year
description: The Federal Government Fiscal Year of the grant program funding opportunity. The Fiscal Year runs from October 1 to September 30. For Disaster Grant Programs, this field represents the Federal Government Fiscal Year in which the disaster was declared. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: region
title: Region
description: Number (1-10) used to represent the Region associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: applicantUei
title: Applicant UEI
description: Single-value that uniquely identifies the applicant/grantee. The Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) is a 12-character alphanumeric ID assigned to an entity in SAM.gov to identify businesses and other entities that do business with the federal government. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: applicantName
title: Applicant Name
description: Name of the applicant requesting Hazard Mitigation Grant funding (e.g., Illinois Emergency Management Agency). An applicant becomes a recipient when it receives a Federal award directly from a Federal awarding agency to carry out an activity under a Federal program. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: countyCode
title: FIPS County Code
description: FIPS three-digit numeric code used to identify counties and county equivalents in the United States, the District of Columbia, US territories, outlying areas of the US and freely associated states. Please note that Indian Reservations are not counties and thus will not have a FIPS county code. Multiple counties may exist and are delimited with a pipe (|) character.

name: subapplicantUei
title: Subapplicant UEI
description: Single-value that uniquely identifies the subapplicant/subgrantee. The Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) is a 12-character alphanumeric ID assigned to an entity in SAM.gov to identify businesses and other entities that do business with the federal government. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subapplicantName
title: Subapplicant Name
description: Name of the Subapplicant requesting Hazard Mitigation Grant funding (e.g., City of Chicago). A Subapplicant becomes a Subrecipient (previously termed Subgrantee) when it receives a subaward from a pass-through entity (i.e., Recipient) to carry out part of a Federal award. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: subapplicantCity
title: Subapplicant City
description: Name of the City (e.g., Chicago) associated with the subapplicant/subrecipient. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subapplicantState
title: Subapplicant State
description: Full name of the State (e.g., Illinois) associated with the subapplicant/subrecipient. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: subapplicantStateAbbreviation
title: Subapplicant State Abbreviation
description: Two letter abbreviation of the State (e.g., IL represents Illinois) associated with the subapplicant/subrecipient. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: subapplicantZipCode
title: Subapplicant Zip Code
description: Five digit ZIP Code associated with the subapplicant/subrecipient (e.g., 60614). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subapplicantZip4
title: Subapplicant Zip 4
description: Four digits that designate a specific location within the ZIP Code associated with the subapplicant/subrecipient (e.g., 0001). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subjectEO12372
title: Subject EO12372
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient is subject to review by Executive Order 12372, Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs. For more information on Executive Order 12372, seehttps://www.archives.gov/federal-register/codification/executive-order/12372.html. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: eo12372ReviewDate
title: EO12372 Review Date
description: Date the subapplication/subgrant was made available to the Executive Order 12372 for review. This is a conditional field in the Subapplicant Information section that is dependent on Subject EO12372 being Yes. While this value may contain time information (00:00:00.000), these are system generated and do not reflect the actual time associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subapplicantFederalDebt
title: Subapplicant Federal Debt
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient is delinquent on any federal debt. Delinquent debt applies to the applicant organization and not to individual people who work on or sign the application. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: dateInitiatedInSystem
title: Date Initiated In System
description: Date and time the project was initiated in the system. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: dateSubmittedToApplicant
title: Date Submitted To Applicant
description: Date and time the subapplication was submitted to the applicant/recipient. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: dateSubmittedToFema
title: Date Submitted To FEMA
description: Date and time the project was submitted to FEMA by the applicant/recipient. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: subapplicationTitle
title: Subapplication Title
description: Title of the subapplication submitted to FEMA by the subapplicant. This field may be altered by FEMA to remove Personal Identifiable Information (PII). If PII is removed, it will be replaced by "[REDACTED]". This is a required field for subapplicants in FEMA GO. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: proposedProjectStartDate
title: Proposed Project Start Date
description: Proposed start date of the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant schedule, which may differ from the official Period of Performance. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: proposedProjectEndDate
title: Proposed Project End Date
description: Proposed end date of the subapplication/subgrant schedule which may differ from the official Period of Performance. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: estimatedTotalDuration
title: Estimated Total Duration
description: Estimated total duration of the subapplication/subgrant in number of months which may differ from the official Period of Performance. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: fundingCategory
title: Funding Category
description: Grant program funding category selected by the Applicant/Recipient for the subapplication/subgrant. The funding categories differ for each grant program and are outlined in the Fiscal Year Notice of Funding Opportunity. For more information on funding categories for each grant program, visithttps://www.grants.gov/. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: subapplicantType
title: Subapplicant Type
description: Type of subapplicant/subrecipient, self-designated by the subapplicant/subrecipient. A subapplicant/subrecipient can be Federally Recognized Tribes, State Agencies, Private Non-Profits, Tribal Agencies, Local Governments/Communities. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: status
title: Status
description: Current status of the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant in the system (e.g., Ineligible, Not Selected, Subaward Offered, Subaward Selected, Submitted to FEMA, etc.). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: subapplicationType
title: Subapplication Type
description: Type of subapplication/subgrant (e.g., Management cost, Plan, Project, Project Scoping, Technical Assistance, etc.). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: benefitingCounties
title: Benefiting Counties
description: County or County equivalent entity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Multiple counties are possible and are delimited by a semicolon. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: primaryActivity
title: Primary Activity
description: Primary mitigation activity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: primarySubactivity
title: Primary Subactivity
description: Primary mitigation subactivity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Primary Activities have a Primary Subactivity. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: secondaryActivity
title: Secondary Activity
description: Secondary mitigation activity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: secondarySubactivity
title: Secondary Subactivity
description: Secondary mitigation subactivity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Secondary Activities have a Secondary Subactivity. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: tertiaryActivity
title: Tertiary Activity
description: Tertiary mitigation activity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: tertiarySubactivity
title: Tertiary Subactivity
description: Tertiary mitigation subactivity associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Tertiary Activities have a Tertiary Subactivity. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: primaryCommunityLifeline
title: Primary Community Lifeline
description: Primary Community Lifeline associated with the subapplication/subgrant. For more information regarding community lifelines, seehttps://www.fema.gov/sw/emergency-managers/practitioners/lifelines. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: primaryCommunityLifelineComponent
title: Primary Community Lifeline Component
description: Primary Community Lifeline Component associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Community Lifelines have a Component. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: secondaryCommunityLifeline
title: Secondary Community Lifeline
description: Secondary Community Lifeline associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: secondaryCommunityLifelineComponent
title: Secondary Community Lifeline Component
description: Secondary Community Lifeline Component associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Community Lifelines have a Component. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: tertiaryCommunityLifeline
title: Tertiary Community Lifeline
description: Tertiary Community Lifeline associated with the subapplication/subgrant. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: tertiaryCommunityLifelineComponent
title: Tertiary Community Lifeline Component
description: Tertiary Community Lifeline Component associated with the subapplication/subgrant. Not all Community Lifelines have a Component. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: primaryHazard
title: Primary Hazard
description: Primary hazard associated with the subapplication/subgrant (e.g., Flooding, Fire, Tornado, etc.). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: secondaryHazard
title: Secondary Hazard
description: Secondary hazard associated with the subapplication/subgrant (e.g., Flooding, Fire, Tornado, etc.). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: tertiaryHazard
title: Tertiary Hazard
description: Tertiary hazard associated with the subapplication/subgrant (e.g., Flooding, Fire, Tornado, etc.). [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: natureBasedSolution
title: Nature-Based Solution
description: The type of nature-based solution associated with the subapplication/subgrant.  Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1' and No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: smallImpoverished
title: Small Impoverished
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient self-identified as a Small Impoverished Community as defined by 42 U.S.C. 5133(a), and in FY2023 the question was expanded to include an OR statement for Community Disaster Resilience Zones (CDRZs) as defined by 42 U.S. Code 5136(a). Under the HMA Grant Programs "Small Impoverished Community" is synonymous with "Economically Disadvantaged Rural Community". Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: populationAffected
title: Population Affected
description: Percentage of population affected by the subapplication/subgrant. This value is self-reported by the subapplicant/subrecipient. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: phasedProject
title: Phased Project
description: Indicates if the subapplication/subgrant is phased. Complex mitigation projects can be phased which enables the Subapplicant/Subrecipient to develop technical and environmental information, including design, engineering studies, and permitting, before FEMA approves funding for full construction. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: construction
title: Construction
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient proposes to perform construction activities under this subapplication/subgrant. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: priorSubapplication
title: Prior Subapplication
description: Indicates if the subapplication/subgrant was created from a prior FEMA HMA Advance Assistance or Project Scoping award or any other federal grant award, or the Subapplicant is a past recipient of Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities non-financial Direct Technical Assistance. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: communityRatingSystem
title: Community Rating System (CRS)
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient participates in FEMA's Community Rating System (CRS). For more information regarding CRS, seehttps://www.fema.gov/floodplain-management/community-rating-system. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: cooperatingTechnicalPartner
title: Cooperating Technical Partner (CTP)
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient participates in the Cooperating Technical Partner (CTP) program. For more information regarding CTP, visithttps://www.fema.gov/flood-maps/cooperating-technical-partners. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: adoptedIcc
title: Adopted International Building Codes (ICC)
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient adopted building codes are consistent with International Code Council's (ICC) building codes. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: yearBuildingCode
title: Year Building Code
description: Year of the Subapplicant/Subrecipient's building code. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: buildingCodesOnBcegs
title: Building Codes Assessed on Building Codes Effectiveness Grading Schedule (BCEGS)
description: Indicates if the Subapplicant/Subrecipient's building codes are assessed on the Building Codes Effectiveness Grading Schedule (BCEGS). For more information regarding BCEGS, seehttps://www.fema.gov/glossary/bcegs. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: bcegsRating
title: Building Codes Effectiveness Grading Schedule (BCEGS) Rating
description: Number (1-10) used to represent the subapplicant/subrecipient's Building Codes Effectiveness Grading Schedule (BCEGS) rating. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: mitigationPlanCovered
title: Mitigation Plan Covered
description: Indicates if the subapplication/subgrant activity is covered by a current FEMA approved multi-hazard mitigation plan in compliance with 44 CFR Part 201. For more information regarding Mitigation Planning, seehttps://www.fema.gov/emergency-managers/risk-management/hazard-mitigation-planning. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: mitigationPlanType
title: Mitigation Plan Type
description: Type of mitigation plan that covers the subapplication/subgrant activity. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: mitigationPlanSubtype
title: Mitigation Plan Subtype
description: Indicates if the mitigation plan, that covers the subapplicant/subgrant activity, for the State/Territory/Tribal Mitigation Plan Types is enhanced or standard. Local Mitigation Plan Types do not have a subtype. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: dateMitigationPlanApproved
title: Date Mitigation Plan Approved
description: Date the mitigation plan covering the subapplication/subgrant activity was approved. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: costEffectivenessMethod
title: Cost-Effectiveness Method
description: Method used to evaluate the subapplication/subgrant's cost-effectiveness. Mitigation activities are required by statute and regulation to be cost-effective, and the determination is performed in a variety of ways (e.g., FEMA BCA Toolkit, pre-calculated benefits, other BCA methodology approved by FEMA). [Source: FEMA GO]

name: preCalculatedBenefit
title: Pre-Calculated Benefit
description: Type of pre-calculated benefit used to determine the subapplication/subgrant's cost-effectiveness (e.g., Acquisitions in the special flood hazard area, Residential hurricane wind retrofits, etc.). For more information on pre-calculated benefits, seehttps://www.fema.gov/grants/guidance-tools/benefit-cost-analysis/streamlined-bca#pre-calculated-benefits. [Source FEMA GO]

name: environmentalBenefit
title: Environmental Benefit
description: Indicates if environmental benefits were added to the benefits in the Benefit-Cost Analysis. Environmental benefits capture the benefits resulting from mitigation activities that improve or preserve the natural environment, such as acquisitions, relocations, and floodplain and stream restoration. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO]

name: seaLevelRise
title: Sea Level Rise
description: Indicates if sea level rise was incorporated into the flood elevations in the Benefit-Cost Analysis. Sea level rise benefits capture the cost associated with elevation/acquisition projects against anticipated flooding due to rising sea levels. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO]

name: socialBenefit
title: Social Benefit
description: Indicates if social benefits were added to the benefits in the Benefit-Cost Analysis. Social benefits capture the avoided costs associated with mental stress, anxiety, and lost wages that disaster survivors would otherwise experience. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: mitigatingProjectSiteInventory
title: Mitigating Project Site Inventory
description: Indicates if the subapplication/subgrant proposes to mitigate project site inventory (e.g., buildings, vacant land, infrastructure/utility/other locations). Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO]

name: projectSiteInventoryLocationKnown
title: Project Site Inventory Location Known
description: Indicates if the location of the project site inventory is known at the time of submission. Examples of unknown locations at time of submission include, but are not limited to, saferoom/shelter lottery subapplication/subgrants. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. [Source FEMA GO]

name: numberBuildingLocations
title: Number of Building Locations
description: For FEMA GO, this value represents the number of building locations proposed to be mitigated. For eGrants and NEMIS, this value may include vacant land and/or infrastructure.  [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: numberInfrastructureLocations
title: Number of Infrastructure Locations
description: Number of infrastructure/utility/other locations proposed to be mitigated. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: numberVacantLandLocations
title: Number of Vacant Land Locations
description: Number of vacant land locations proposed to be mitigated. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: federalShareAmount
title: Federal Share Amount
description: Cost share amount in dollars requested/approved for the subapplication/subgrant to be covered by FEMA. In general, HMA funds may be used to pay up to 75 percent of the eligible activity costs. For more information regarding cost sharing, seehttps://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation/hazard-mitigation-assistance-guidance. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: nonFederalShareAmount
title: Non-Federal Share Amount
description: Cost share amount in dollars requested/approved for the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant to be covered by Non-Federal sources. Contributions of cash, third-party in-kind services, materials, or any combination thereof, may be accepted as part of the Non-Federal cost share. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: mgmtFederalShareAmount
title: Management Federal Share Amount
description: Cost share amount in dollars requested/approved for the management costs to be covered by FEMA. For more information regarding cost sharing, seehttps://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation/hazard-mitigation-assistance-guidance. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: mgmtNonFederalShareAmount
title: Management Non-Federal Share Amount
description: Cost share amount in dollars requested/approved for the management costs to be covered by Non-Federal sources. For more information regarding cost sharing, seehttps://www.fema.gov/grants/mitigation/hazard-mitigation-assistance-guidance. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: totalSubapplicationAmount
title: Total Subapplication Amount
description: Total amount in dollars requested/approved for the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant. The total cost to implement approved mitigation activities is generally funded by a combination of Federal and Non-Federal sources. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: totalObligatedAmount
title: Total Obligated Amount
description: Total federal amount obligated for the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant. Obligations are executed in increments, based on the subgrant meeting an established project milestone schedule, until the subgrant or grant is completed. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: totalPaymentAmount
title: Total Payment Amount
description: Total amount in dollars for payments for the subgrant or grant. A payment is requested by the applicant/recipient for reimbursement of eligible activity costs. [Source: FEMA GO]

name: federalSharePercentage
title: Federal Share Percentage
description: Percentage of the project cost to be covered by FEMA. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: nonFederalSharePercentage
title: Non-Federal Share Percentage
description: Percentage of the project cost to be covered by Non-Federal sources. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: benefitCostRatio
title: Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR)
description: Numerical expression of the cost-effectiveness of the subapplication/subgrant as submitted by the subapplicant (i.e., not FEMA validated). The Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) is derived from a subapplication's total net benefits divided by its total cost. Composite BCRs of 1.0 or greater have more benefits than costs and are therefore cost-effective. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: bcaTotalBenefits
title: BCA Total Benefits
description: Anticipated benefits that occur for the life of the project used to derive the Benefit-Cost Ratio to demonstrate cost-effectiveness. Benefits may include avoided damage, loss of function, and displacement. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: bcaTotalCosts
title: BCA Total Costs
description: Total costs of the subapplication/subgrant used to derive the Benefit-Cost Ratio to demonstrate cost-effectiveness. The BCA Total Costs may differ from the Total Subapplication Amount due to costs not required to be included in the Benefit-Cost Analysis. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants, NEMIS]

name: disasterNumber
title: Disaster Number
description: Sequentially assigned number used to designate an event or incident declared as a disaster. For more information on the disaster process,https://www.fema.gov/disasters/how-declared. [Source: FEMA GO, NEMIS]

name: selectionStatus
title: Selection Status
description: The status of the subapplication/subgrant assigned by the Program during the Selection Phase (e.g., Identified for Further Review, Not Selected, Did Not Meet HMA Requirements, etc.). The selection statuses are outlined in the Fiscal Year Notice of Funding Opportunity. For more information, visithttps://www.grants.gov/. This information may differ from the formal selection announcement made by FEMA following the close of the application period. [Source: Program Derived]

name: selectionFundingCategory
title: Selection Funding Category
description: Grant program funding category assigned by the Program for the subapplication/subgrant. The funding categories differ for each grant program and are outlined in the Fiscal Year Notice of Funding Opportunity. For more information on funding categories for each grant program, visithttps://www.grants.gov/. This value may differ from the Funding Category field. This information may differ from the formal selection announcement made by FEMA following the close of the application period. [Source: Program Derived]

name: selectionProgramActivity
title: Selection Program Activity
description: Grant program funding category activity assigned by the Program for the subapplication/subgrant. The funding categories differ for each grant program and are outlined in the Fiscal Year Notice of Funding Opportunity. For more information on funding categories for each grant program, visithttps://www.grants.gov/. This value may differ from the Funding Category field. This information may differ from the formal selection announcement made by FEMA following the close of the application period. [Source: Program Derived]

name: selectionFederalShareAmount
title: Selection Federal Share Amount
description: Cost share amount in dollars approved during the Selection Phase for the subapplication/subgrant or application/grant to be covered by FEMA. This value may differ from the Federal Share Amount field. This is a conditional field that is dependent when Selection Status is 'Identified for Further Review'. This information may differ from the formal selection announcement made by FEMA following the close of the application period. [Source: Program Derived]

name: selectionFundCode
title: Selection Fund Code
description: Fund code assigned by the Program for the subapplication/subgrant. The possible codes include 5 (National Flood Insurance Fund, National Flood Insurance Act of 1968), IN (National Flood Insurance Fund, Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act), 6M (Disaster Relief Fund, Disaster Recovery Reform Act of 2018), and 6N (Disaster Relief Fund, Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act). [Source: Program Derived]

name: jurisdictionStatus
title: Jurisdiction Status
description: The status of a Jurisdiction that is an identified participant in a Mitigation Plan. Jurisdiction status values include: Approved, Approved Pending Adoption (APA), Plan In Progress, In Review, Expired, Awaiting Revisions

name: crsRating
title: CRS Rating
description: Number (1-9) used to represent the Subapplicant/Subrecipient's Community Rating System Class. See https://www.fema.gov/floodplain-management/community-rating-system for more details. [Source: FEMA GO, eGrants]

name: elevationDifference
title: Elevation Difference
description:
Difference between the elevation of the lowest floor used for rating, or the floodproofed elevation, and the base flood elevation (BFE), or base flood depth, as appropriate. Round to nearest higher elevation difference in whole feet using .5 as the midpoint

NOTE: The depth shown on the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Zone AO that indicates the depth of water above the highest adjacent grade resulting from a flood that has a 1% chance of equaling or exceeding that level in any given year. The elevation of surface water resulting from a flood that has a 1% chance of equaling or exceeding that level in any given year. The BFE is shown on the FloodInsurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Zones AE, AH, A1-A30, AR, AR/A, AR/AE, AR/A1-A30, AR/AH, AR/A0, V1-V30 andVE.
The value of 9999.0 indicates the field is not reported and/or used for this policy.

name: sanctionDate
title: Sanction Date
description:
Represents the effective date a community was penalized for non-compliance with NFIP minimum standards and requirements and may include a sanction reason code following the date:
(S) denotes Suspension. Refers to the formal process by which a communitys eligibility to participate in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) is revoked due to failure to comply with required floodplain management regulations or enforcement standards. During suspension, the community loses the ability to sell or renew flood insurance policies under the NFIP.
(W) denotes Withdrawn. Refers to the process by which a community voluntarily removes itself from participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). This is accomplished by submitting a certified legislative action explicitly stating the communitys intent to withdraw. Upon receipt and verification of this action, FEMA formally withdraws the community from the NFIP and publishes notice of the withdrawal in the Federal Register. Once withdrawn, the community loses eligibility to sell or renew NFIP flood insurance policies.

name: nfipRl
title: NFIP RL
description: National Flood Insurance Program insurance-relaled Repetitive Loss. An NFIP-insured structure with two or more claims/losses resulting in claim payments (including building and contents) totaling more than $1000 per claim that are recorded in any 10-year period. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. When mitigated, this value may change from true to false

name: nfipSrl
title: NFIP SRL
description: National Flood Insurance Program insurance-related Severe Repetitive Loss. An NFIP-Insured structure that has incurred flood-related damage for which four or more separate claims payments have been made, with the amount of each claim (including building and contents payments) exceeding $5,000, and with the cumulative amount of such claims payments exceeding $20,000; or for which at least two separate claims payments (building payments only) have been made under such coverage, with the cumulative amount of such claims exceeding the market value of the building. In both instances, at least two of the claims must be within 10 years of each other, and claims made within 10 days of each other will be counted as one claim. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. When mitigated, this value may change from true to false.

name: fmaRl
title: FMA RL
description: Flood Mitigation Assistance (grant-related) Repetitive Loss. An NFIP-insured structure that has incurred flood-related damage on 2 occasions, in which the cost of repair, on the average, equaled or exceeded 25 percent of the value of the structure at the time of each such flood event. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'.

name: fmaSrl
title: FMA SRL
description: Flood Mitigation Assistance (grant-related) Severe Repetitive Loss. An NFIP-Insured structure that has incurred flood-related damage for which four or more separate claims payments have been made, with the amount of each claim (including building and contents payments) exceeding $5,000, and with the cumulative amount of such claims payments exceeding $20,000; or for which at least two separate claims payments (building payments only) have been made under such coverage, with the cumulative amount of such claims exceeding the market value of the building. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'.

name: postFIRMConstructionIndicator
title: Post FIRM Construction Indicator
description: Yes (Y) or No (N) Indicator on whether construction was started before or after publication of the FIRM. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'. For insurance rating purposes, buildings for which the start of construction or substantial improvement was after December 31, 1974, or on or after the effective date of the initial FIRM for the community, whichever is later, are considered Post-FIRM construction

name: primaryResidenceIndicator
title: Primary Residence Indicator
description:
Indicates whether or not the insured building/condominium unit is the primary residence of the insured. Yes is indicated with either a 'true' or '1'. No is indicated with either a 'false' or '0'.
A single-family dwelling/condominium unit qualifies as the primary residence of the insured provided that, at the time of loss, the named insured or the named insured's spouse has lived in the dwelling for either (1) 80 percent of the 365 days immediately preceding the loss, or (2) 80 percent of the period of ownership of the insured dwelling, if ownership is less than 365 days. 
Effective June 1, 2014, the NFIP defines primary residence to be a building that will be lived in by the insured or the insureds spouse for more than 50 percent of the 365 days following the policy effective date.

name: mitigatedIndicator

name: insuredIndicator
